images.title: Each place value is nines plus one
images.purpose: Shows that each hundred is 99 plus 1 and each ten is 9 plus 1, so the leftovers of 427 are its digits.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. Three groups in one row: hundreds, tens and ones, with a sum of the leftovers underneath.
images.exact_structure: Group 1, labelled 4 hundreds above: 4 tall teal (#0072B2) bars, each labelled 99, each with one small amber (#E69F00) square on top. Group 2, labelled 2 tens above: 2 short teal (#0072B2) bars, each labelled 9, each with one small amber (#E69F00) square on top. Group 3, labelled 7 ones above: 7 small amber (#E69F00) squares in a row. All amber squares are the same size: 13 in all. Below the groups, centred: 4 + 2 + 7 = 13. Under it, in a reddish purple (#CC79A7) box: remainder 4. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Every place value leaves 1 on division by 9, so 427 leaves the same remainder as 4 + 2 + 7 = 13, which is 4.

image_decisions.why: Bars of nines with one leftover square per place value make the digit sum rule visible.
